data.hypothesis: A 1536-source tile paired with the existing 256-target CTA may reduce repeated global source-field loads while using 24,576 bytes of shared memory, below the 49,152-byte limit. The larger tile may reduce staging-loop overhead versus smaller tiles, but added shared-memory use and barriers may offset that benefit; timing must decide.
data.notes: This is one candidate in the tile-size sweep, using the existing matching block and items_per_block values of 256, so launch.json is unchanged. The supplied observations include a correct baseline (mean 0.0018526411283622502 s) and correct prior candidates, but provide no per-size breakdown. This candidate has not been measured; rely on controller correctness checks and the official per-size geometric-mean timing protocol.
transformations: Cooperatively stage up to 1536 source particles' x, y, z, and mass fields in shared memory per CTA, using four arrays totaling 24,576 bytes.
Keep 256 target threads per CTA, retain one thread per target and the original force evaluation order and arithmetic, and exclude self-interactions.
Mask target tails without allowing threads to exit before CTA barriers, and limit each source tile to the remaining valid particles.
